ai.description: The Deccan Fan-throated Lizard reaches 7–8 cm. It is brown with a dark lateral stripe. Males possess a distinctive, vibrant blue-and-black throat fan used for territorial display.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the male’s throat fan (dewlap), which features a distinct, vibrant blue patch bordered by a bold black band, unlike the patterns of other species.
ai.habitat: *Sarada deccanensis* inhabits open, arid, and rocky landscapes within the Deccan Plateau, typically found in dry deciduous scrublands and grasslands at low elevations.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, males perform conspicuous displays by extending a vibrant, fan-like throat pouch (dewlap) to attract mates and defend their territory.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sarada deccanensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–6 eggs. Breeding occurs annually during the monsoon season, generally from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sarada deccanensis* is endemic to the Deccan Plateau in India, primarily occurring across the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana at low to mid-elevations.
